docs.title: Thermodynamic Waddington Pipeline
docs.text:
Non-equilibrium thermodynamics of single-cell fate.

Trajectory tools tell you where a cell is going. This pipeline asks how far from equilibrium the journey is, with an irreversibility measure that is calibrated on ground truth (it does not false-positive on reversible flow), a committor commitment coordinate, and a free-energy landscape in kT.

docs.title: Why it exists
docs.text: Differentiation is a driven, non-equilibrium process. The standard single-cell toolkit (scVelo, CellRank, Palantir, Waddington-OT) measures its geometry - order, fate probabilities, transport. None of them measures its irreversibility. A process can be well-ordered yet close to equilibrium, or strongly driven and dissipative; the difference is the entropy production, a central quantity of stochastic thermodynamics. Measuring it correctly from a velocity field is harder than it looks: the naive estimator over-detects, and this package replaces it with a calibrated one.

docs.title: What you get
docs.text:
• A calibrated irreversibility measure. A discrete Hodge decomposition splits the velocity flow into a gradient (reversible) and a cyclic (irreversible) part; the cyclic fraction is ~0 for reversible flow and rises with real circulation. AUROC 1.00 on equilibrium-vs-driven ground truth, where the naive entropy-production permutation test false-positives every time.
  • Robust to noise and sequencing depth. A noise-matched null built from the data's own noise: false positives 100% -> 0% on noisy ground truth.
  • Validated across two phyla. Pancreas, gastrulation and bone marrow (vertebrate) and Drosophila spermatogenesis (Fly Cell Atlas, velocity built from the raw reads, FlyBase-linked genes).
  • A free-energy landscape on a physical kT scale, from a Jarzynski path-work functional and a density-anchored Boltzmann inversion.
  • A commitment coordinate. The transition-path-theory committor, which locates where fate commits and gives a commitment free-energy barrier in kT.
  • Cycle-resolved irreversibility (Schnakenberg cycle affinities in kT), MFPT commitment timescales, and optimal-transport chaining across stages.

docs.title: Thirty-second example
docs.text:
from thermodynamic_waddington import analyze

report = analyze(expression, velocity, labels=labels,
                 source_labels=["Ductal"], target_labels=["Beta"])

report.irreversibility_cyclic_fraction   # ~0 reversible, higher = circulation
report.irreversibility_cycle_affinity_kt # the same in kT (Schnakenberg)
report.commitment_label         # where fate commits
report.commitment_barrier_kt    # how hard, in kT

docs.title: Honesty note
docs.text: This package is deliberate about its domain. Its methodological result is a correct irreversibility readout: the calibrated measure shows real developmental lineages are close to reversible (gradient-like), which corrects an earlier reading of the naive entropy-production test. Its committor ordering advantage is real on some datasets and not others. All of that is in Limitations and scope, because a method you can trust is one that tells you where it fails.

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: The public surface. Import everything from the top level: from thermodynamic_waddington import ....

docs.title: analyze(expression, velocity, labels=None, source_labels=None, target_labels=None, config=None, significance=0.05) -> AnalysisReport
docs.text: Runs the pipeline end to end and returns the headline results. Pass labels plus source_labels (progenitor) and target_labels (terminal) to also get the committor commitment coordinate and barrier.

docs.title: analyze_adata(adata, velocity_layer="velocity", expression_layer=None, label_key=None, source=None, target=None, config=None, n_top_genes=50, key_added="tw") -> AnalysisReport
docs.text: The same, directly on an AnnData. Reads the velocity layer (or derives an unspliced-minus-spliced proxy), uses the top-n_top_genes by variance, and writes the per-cell committor, energy, and irreversibility map to adata.obs['{key_added}_committor'], adata.obs['{key_added}_energy'], and adata.obs['{key_added}_irreversibility'], plus the magnitude-invariant adata.obs['{key_added}_cyclic_fraction'] and the noise-matched adata.obs['{key_added}_cyclic_excess'], with the report in adata.uns['{key_added}'].

docs.title: AnalysisReport
docs.text: Dataclass with: n_cells, n_edges, n_attractors, irreversibility_cyclic_fraction, irreversibility_cycle_affinity_kt, irreversibility_noise_matched_excess, irreversibility_noise_matched_z, landscape_range_kt, path_vs_density_r2, committor_order, commitment_label, commitment_barrier_kt, transition_state_q, warnings, and the legacy entropy_production_rate, entropy_production_pvalue, is_irreversible (kept for comparison; that test over-detects). Methods: to_dict(), save(path).

docs.title: Plotting
docs.text:
from thermodynamic_waddington import plots (needs matplotlib):

  • plots.committor(values, coords, ax=None) - scatter colored by the committor.
  • plots.landscape(energies, coords, ax=None) - scatter colored by free energy.
  • plots.free_energy_profile(values, temperature=1.0, ax=None) - the commitment barrier curve.

coords is any n-by-2 array: a UMAP, a PCA embedding, or fit.embedding.

docs.title: fit_landscape(expression, velocity, config=None, labels=None, ...) -> LandscapeFit
docs.text: The full pipeline. Returns a LandscapeFit with energies, attractors, edges, barriers, embedding, and a large diagnostics dict (entropy production, Schnakenberg, spectral, and more). LandscapeFit.save/load persist it as JSON.

docs.title: FitConfig
docs.text: All numerical settings: neighbors, dimensions, temperature, velocity_scale, max_paths, bootstrap and permutation replicate counts, enable_cycle_decomposition, enable_entropy_production, seed, and more. FitConfig().validate(n_cells, n_features) checks inputs.

docs.title: developmental_coordinate(fit, source_labels, target_labels, iterations=400) -> list[float]
docs.text: Per-cell committor: 0 at progenitor states, 1 at terminal fates.

docs.title: commitment_profile(fit, source_labels, target_labels) -> CommitmentReport
docs.text: Orders cell types by mean committor and locates commitment (order, mean_committor, commitment_label, peak_flux_label).

docs.title: committor_free_energy_profile(committor, temperature=1.0, grid=60) -> FreeEnergyProfile
docs.text: Potential of mean force along the committor. Returns q_grid, free_energy_kt, barrier_kt, barrier_q.

docs.title: irreversibility.cyclic_irreversibility(pts, vels, graph, bootstrap=0, seed=0) -> IrreversibilityReport
docs.text: Calibrated irreversibility: the cyclic (non-gradient) energy fraction of the velocity flow from a discrete Hodge decomposition (cyclic_fraction, bootstrap_ci, n_pairs, n_cells). Sparse least-squares, O(edges).

docs.title: irreversibility.cycle_affinities(pts, vels, graph, temperature=1.0, velocity_scale=1.0) -> CycleAffinityReport
docs.text: Schnakenberg cycle affinities in kT (n_cycles, rms_affinity_kt, max_affinity_kt, mean_abs_affinity_kt).

docs.title: irreversibility.noise_matched_irreversibility(pts, vels, graph, draws=10, references=5, seed=0, per_cell=False)
docs.text: Cyclic fraction against a null carrying the data's own noise (reversible velocity from the best-fitting potential, plus residuals re-drawn among neighbours with random signs), bias-corrected on reversible-by-construction references. Returns NoiseMatchedReport (cyclic_fraction, null_mean, bias, excess, z, and per_cell_excess when per_cell=True). Use it whenever velocity noise or sequencing depth varies across the data.

docs.title: irreversibility.cyclic_fraction_per_cell(pts, vels, graph)
docs.text: Per-cell cyclic fraction in [0, 1]: on each cell's edges, cyclic energy over cyclic plus gradient energy. Invariant to velocity magnitude, so regions with different sequencing depth compare on one scale. Read it against the same function applied to a gradient field on the same cells (the local floor).

docs.title: irreversibility.cyclic_flow_per_cell(pts, vels, graph)
docs.text: Per-cell share of the cyclic flow energy. It also grows with velocity magnitude, so it can track sequencing depth; prefer cyclic_fraction_per_cell to compare regions.

docs.title: estimate_entropy_production(points, velocity, densities, diffusions, graph, config) -> EntropyProductionReport
docs.text: Legacy Seifert entropy-production rate with bootstrap CIs and a permutation null (entropy_production_rate, permutation_p_value, bootstrap_ci, null_mean). Kept for comparison: it is significant on reversible ground truth, so do not use it alone for irreversibility claims.

docs.title: calibrate_fit(fit) -> CalibrationReport · calibrate(path_energies, coords)
docs.text: Density-anchored kT calibration (boltzmann_energy_range_kt, r_squared, kt_per_work_unit). boltzmann_free_energy(coords) returns the kT landscape; basin_barriers_kt(energies, labels) gives per-type depths.

docs.title: estimate_mfpt(edges, energies, attractors, temperature=1.0) -> MFPTResult
docs.text: Mean first-passage times and per-cell commitment times.

docs.title: Optimal transport
docs.text: sinkhorn, fit_schrodinger_chain, displacement_interpolate, estimate_growth_weights - work-cost optimal transport chained across stages.

docs.title: export.export_cells(expression, velocity, labels, source_labels, target_labels, out_dir, prefix="tw", coords=None, cell_ids=None, stage_order=None, ...) -> ExportResult
docs.text: Runs the calibrated readouts on one lineage and writes <prefix>_cells.csv (one row per cell: tw_id, tw_text, tw_stage, tw_x, tw_y, tw_committor, tw_phase, tw_energy, tw_cyclic_fraction, tw_cyclic_excess, tw_downstream) and <prefix>_summary.json (commitment stage, barrier and its PMF curve, phase counts, per-stage means, noise-matched irreversibility, and a description of every column). The tw-export command does the same from an .h5ad.

docs.title: Data
docs.text: make_synthetic_dataset(cells, genes, seed) -> SyntheticDataset for a labeled synthetic dataset with expression, velocity, and lineage labels.

docs.title: Command line
docs.text: Console scripts installed with the package include twaddington (fit / report / audit), tw-real (real-data ingest and validation), and tw-benchmark. Run any with --help.

docs.title: Benchmarks and validation
docs.text: Every number here reproduces with python benchmarks/run_all.py. Results are reported straight, negatives included.

docs.title: Irreversibility, measured correctly
docs.text:
Two ways to ask "is the differentiation irreversible", with different answers.

The naive test over-detects. The density-based Seifert entropy-production permutation test (shuffle velocity across cells) reaches AUROC 1.00 against that control, but so does a one-line velocity-coherence score, because the shuffle destroys all velocity structure, not just irreversibility. On a synthetic equilibrium field whose true entropy production is zero it fires every time (false-positive rate 1.0; AUROC 0.44 for equilibrium vs non-equilibrium). It is detecting velocity-position coupling, not broken detailed balance.

The calibrated measure. irreversibility.cyclic_irreversibility splits the velocity flow (discrete Hodge decomposition) into a gradient (reversible) part and a cyclic (irreversible) part and reports the cyclic energy fraction. On the same ground truth it is calibrated: an equilibrium floor of 0.12 rising monotonically to 0.85 under a known rotational drive, AUROC 1.00 separating equilibrium from non-equilibrium where coherence sits at 0.53. benchmarks/synthetic_ground_truth.py.

What the real tissues show (reported straight). On real proxy velocity the three developmental lineages are close to gradient-like:

tissue cyclic fraction clean floor excess over clean floor noise-matched excess pancreas endocrine 0.151 0.099 +0.051 -0.011 (z = -1.0) gastrulation erythroid 0.080 0.085 -0.005 -0.005 (z = -0.5) bone marrow erythroid 0.108 0.097 +0.012 -0.010 (z = -0.8) fly testis germline 0.097 0.086 +0.011 -0.007 (z = -0.6)

Against the clean floor pancreas looked like it carried a modest excess; against the noise-matched null (below) it does not, and no lineage does: all four are reversible within their own noise. A linear lineage has an arrow of time but little circulation, so low cyclic entropy production is the expected, correct result. The measure's power is established on the synthetic geometry above (AUROC 1.00); on these near-1D real lineages, even injecting a rotation barely moves the fraction, because a 1D structure has no cycles to carry circulation -- which is itself why the real result sits at the floor. The same holds for the noise-matched readout: injecting rotation into the pancreas geometry moves it only at the strongest drive (+0.010 at w = 2). benchmarks/irreversibility_real.py.

The directional progression is captured by the committor. The strong "irreversible across three tissues" reading of the old permutation test does not survive calibration, and is corrected here. benchmarks/generalization.py.

docs.title: Noise-matched irreversibility (robust to sequencing depth)
docs.text:
The matched gradient floor is a clean radial field: it has no noise. Real velocity does, and noise looks cyclic, so shallow-sequenced or noisy cells read as circulating. noise_matched_irreversibility builds the null from the data itself: a reversible velocity (the local gradient of the potential that best explains the work along each edge) plus the observed residual noise (each cell's velocity minus its neighbourhood mean), re-drawn from neighbouring cells with random signs. Running the identical procedure on reference datasets that are reversible by construction estimates the method's own bias, which is subtracted (a parametric double bootstrap).

benchmarks/noise_matched_ground_truth.py adds measurement noise to the linear diffusion ground truth -- none, uniform, or uneven (half the cells 10x noisier, like shallow cells) -- over 5 drives x 4 noise settings x 10 seeds:

clean-floor excess noise-matched excess false-positive rate at equilibrium, any noise 1.00 0.00 AUROC equilibrium vs driven, pooled over noise 0.76 0.96 noisy equilibrium ranked above a clean weak drive 1.00 0.00 per-cell excess in the noisy half, at equilibrium +0.46 -0.001

Power falls with noise, as it should: under heavy uneven noise a weak drive is no longer detectable, while w >= 1 still is. analyze() reports irreversibility_noise_matched_excess and ..._z; analyze_adata writes the per-cell version to obs['tw_cyclic_excess'].

On the fly germline it settles the spermatid question: the post-meiotic excess of +0.12 over the clean floor becomes -0.010 against the noise-matched null, the per-stage excess no longer tracks depth (Spearman +0.06, was -0.77), and the whole germline is -0.007 (z = -0.6): reversible within its own noise.

docs.title: Drosophila spermatogenesis (a second phylum)
docs.text:
benchmarks/fly_testis.py runs the same calibrated readouts on the male germline of the Fly Cell Atlas testis (Li et al., Science 2022): spermatogonia, the spermatocyte program (stages 0-7a), and elongating spermatids, 7,335 cells with the atlas's own annotation as stage labels. The atlas ships no spliced/unspliced layers, so benchmarks/fly_testis_prepare.py builds them from the raw reads: it streams an evenly spaced sample (61.8M reads, about 10% of library FCA59) out of the unaligned 10x BAMs at ArrayExpress E-MTAB-10519 over HTTP range requests, and quantifies nascent and mature RNA with kallisto | bustools against Ensembl BDGP6.46 (88.6% pseudoaligned). All 15,292 atlas cells in the library match by barcode. Genes carry FlyBase IDs.

readout result velocity sanity check unspliced fraction 0.19 in spermatocytes -> 0.04 in spermatids (5x drop): the known post-meiotic transcription shutdown, recovered from reads quantified here calibrated irreversibility cyclic fraction 0.097 vs reversible floor 0.086 (excess +0.011), shuffled ceiling 0.52; noise-matched excess -0.007 (z = -0.6) -- reversible within its noise, like the vertebrate tissues committor ordering vs stage Spearman 0.78 +/- 0.05 vs PC1 0.47, committor wins 8/8 subsamples where commitment happens inside the spermatocyte program in 7/8 subsamples (spermatocyte 4 to 7a) commitment barrier 2.1 kT [1.6, 2.6], 8 subsamples commitment-driver genes top-50 list overlap between independent fits 0.36 vs 0.011 by chance; a regulator list fixed in advance (tMAC, tTAF, bam/bgcn, spermatid genes) is not enriched (0/14 in the top 5%)

The committor result is the clearest gain: on this long, staged lineage it beats PC1 decisively, unlike gastrulation where PC1 wins. The driver genes (FlyBase links in experiments/fly_testis.json) are a reproducible ranking for follow-up, not causal evidence; the canonical regulators switch on when the spermatocyte program begins, not at its end where commitment sits.

A second artifact, caught. The per-cell cyclic-energy map first showed a 7x peak of circulation in late spermatocytes. That map is an energy, so it grows with velocity magnitude, and spermatocytes are the deepest-sequenced cells: across stages it tracks sequencing depth (Spearman +0.84). The new magnitude-invariant cyclic_fraction_per_cell, read against a per-stage reversible floor on the same cells, removes it: the pre-meiotic germline sits within +0.014 of reversible. The residual post-meiotic excess (+0.12) runs opposite to depth (-0.77) and to the unspliced fraction (-0.75): it appears exactly where the velocity signal vanishes. The noise-matched null (above) confirms it is noise: against it the spermatids read -0.010.

docs.title: Commitment barrier
docs.text: The potential of mean force along the committor gives a commitment barrier of 1.6 kT [1.4, 1.9] on the pancreas branch, with the transition state mid- trajectory. benchmarks/commitment_barrier.py.

docs.title: Physical calibration
docs.text: The landscape is ~5 kT deep on a kT scale; the low path-work-vs-density R^2 (~0.14) quantifies its non-equilibrium departure. benchmarks/free_energy_calibration.py.

docs.title: Developmental ordering (dataset-dependent)
docs.text: On pancreas the committor beats PC1 and an endpoint-informed axis at recovering developmental stage: 0.94 +/- 0.02 vs 0.89, winning 10/10 subsamples, paired Wilcoxon p = 0.002. On the cleaner gastrulation erythroid lineage, plain PC1 wins (0.94 vs 0.81). The committor's ordering advantage is therefore not universal; its value is as a commitment coordinate tied to the thermodynamics. benchmarks/predictive_ordering.py, benchmarks/statistical_validation.py.

docs.title: CellRank comparison
docs.text:
benchmarks/cellrank_comparison.py puts the committor and CellRank on the same footing: both compute the probability of reaching the Beta terminal before falling back to the Ductal progenitor (a two-boundary absorption for CellRank's VelocityKernel + GPCCA, the transition-path committor here) on identical proxy velocity, scored on recovering developmental stage. Run at 2,000 cells (3 seeds), the regime GPCCA is built for:

method abs Spearman with stage CellRank two-boundary absorption 0.99 +/- 0.00 TW committor 0.95 +/- 0.00 PC1 0.94 +/- 0.00

CellRank wins, and it should: on a linear lineage with enough cells its absorption probability is exactly the tool for the job. The committor beats PC1 and tracks CellRank closely, but ordering was never this pipeline's claim. This holds in the low-data regime too: at 150 cells (5 seeds) the two-boundary CellRank is still stable and ahead (0.99 +/- 0.00 vs committor 0.94 +/- 0.03 vs PC1 0.92) -- so there is no small-n advantage for the committor either. A single terminal is degenerate on a linear lineage (CellRank returns probability 1 everywhere), so the comparison uses two boundaries; an earlier 150-cell, single-terminal run gave a noisy, non-meaningful CellRank number and is superseded. The script includes a numpy-2 compatibility shim (for pygpcca) and runs CellRank single-process to avoid a Windows multiprocessing hang. The durable point: CellRank does fate mapping well, and this pipeline adds the calibrated irreversibility measure and kT barrier it does not compute.

docs.title: Performance and scale
docs.text:
Vectorizing the core made fits 2.2x-6.2x faster with bit-identical outputs, and a KD-tree graph handles 50,000 cells in seconds. The full diagnostic fit remains super-linear past a few thousand cells; the graph core is what scales. benchmarks/runtime_scaling.py, benchmarks/scaling.py.

The irreversibility measures scale too. The Hodge cyclic-fraction projection moved from a dense pseudo-inverse (cubic in cells) to a sparse least-squares solve (bit-identical output): 88x faster at 2,000 cells, and the cyclic fraction and cycle affinity both run on 50,000 cells in about six seconds, where the dense projection would take tens of hours. benchmarks/irreversibility_scaling.py.

docs.title: Dynamical velocity
docs.text:
The headline results were re-run on real scVelo dynamical velocity: the committor ordering held (0.98 on pancreas), and one entropy-production run came back non- significant under scVelo's Ms-smoothed representation specifically, which the gene-count and normalization sweeps then bounded. benchmarks/dynamical_velocity_validation.py.

The calibrated measure gives the same answer under both velocity models: on 800 pancreas cells the cyclic-fraction excess over the gradient floor is -0.003 for the proxy and -0.001 for scVelo dynamical velocity, so the near-reversible reading is not an artifact of the proxy. benchmarks/dynamical_cyclic.py.

docs.title: Concepts
docs.text: The science behind each number, in plain terms.

docs.title: The Waddington landscape
docs.text: C. H. Waddington pictured cells as balls rolling downhill into fates. The modern version is quantitative: from single-cell data we estimate an effective free-energy landscape whose valleys are attractor states and whose ridges are barriers between them. This pipeline builds that landscape and, crucially, asks a question the picture leaves out: is the ball actually being pushed, or could it roll back up just as easily?

docs.title: RNA velocity
docs.text: RNA velocity estimates, for each cell, the direction it is moving in gene- expression space, from the ratio of unspliced to spliced transcripts. It turns a static snapshot into a vector field of motion. The pipeline accepts velocity from scVelo's dynamical model, or a transparent unspliced-minus-spliced proxy.

docs.title: Path work and the free-energy landscape
docs.text: Cells are placed on a k-nearest-neighbor graph in PCA space. Each velocity- aligned edge is annotated with a path-work value combining three physical terms: a density ratio, the velocity drift along the edge, and a diffusion noise term. Free energies are then propagated by multi-source Jarzynski exponential averaging, so every cell receives a value from the minimum-work path in its component. This is an effective landscape, not a molecular free energy.

docs.title: Irreversibility - the central quantity
docs.text:
For a system in equilibrium, forward and reverse transitions balance (detailed balance) and no entropy is produced. A driven system breaks that balance.

Why the naive test fails. A natural estimator is Seifert's pair-flux entropy production with a null built by shuffling velocity across cells. But a shuffle destroys all velocity structure, not only broken detailed balance, so the test also fires on a perfectly reversible gradient flow: on synthetic equilibrium ground truth it reports significance every time. It detects velocity-position coupling, not irreversibility. It is kept in the package for comparison only.

The calibrated measure. Any edge flow on a graph splits uniquely (discrete Hodge decomposition) into a gradient part, which is the flow of a potential and is reversible, and a cyclic part, which circulates and is what breaks detailed balance. The cyclic fraction - the share of flow energy in the cyclic part - is ~0 for a conservative field and rises with real circulation. It is validated on a linear diffusion with a known rotational drive (AUROC 1.00, monotonic in the drive). Compare it with a matched gradient floor at the same sample size, since a finite kNN graph gives a small non-zero floor.

docs.title: Schnakenberg cycles
docs.text: Schnakenberg's network theory attributes entropy production to the fundamental cycles of the graph. The pipeline computes the thermodynamic affinity of every cycle, in kT, from a spanning-tree potential: zero for a conservative field (Kolmogorov's criterion), non-zero with circulation. It is a physical-units companion to the cyclic fraction.

docs.title: The committor and commitment
docs.text: The forward committor q(x) is the probability that a cell at state x reaches the terminal fate before returning to the progenitor. It is the principled reaction coordinate of transition-path theory: 0 at the progenitor, 1 at the terminal fate. Where it crosses 0.5 is the point of commitment. The potential of mean force along it, F(q) = -kT ln P(q), gives the commitment barrier in kT.

docs.title: Physical calibration
docs.text: The landscape is placed on a kT scale by a density-anchored Boltzmann inversion, F = -kT ln P over a kernel density of the embedding - the standard Waddington pseudopotential. The agreement (R^2) between the path-work landscape and this equilibrium reference is itself informative: a low value means the flow-based landscape carries non-equilibrium structure the density landscape cannot see.

docs.title: Mean first-passage time
docs.text: MFPT gives the expected number of graph steps for a cell to first reach an attractor (Kemeny-Snell theory), a kinetic commitment timescale that complements the thermodynamic irreversibility measures.

docs.title: References
docs.text: Waddington 1957; Jarzynski 1997; Schnakenberg 1976; Kemeny & Snell 1960; Seifert 2012; E & Vanden-Eijnden 2006; La Manno et al. 2018; Bergen et al. 2020.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Is this a replacement for scVelo or CellRank? No. Those estimate pseudotime, fate probabilities, and transport, and do it well. This adds a complementary layer they do not have: a calibrated measure of how far from equilibrium the process is, and a commitment coordinate with a kT barrier. Use them together.

Do I need RNA velocity? Yes, in some form. Velocity supplies the direction that makes the irreversibility and path-work computations meaningful. You can supply scVelo dynamical velocity or a transparent unspliced-minus-spliced proxy. Without measured velocity the velocity-dependent outputs are disclosed as unavailable.

Which irreversibility number should I report? The calibrated cyclic fraction (report.irreversibility_cyclic_fraction), compared with a matched gradient floor, and optionally the cycle affinity in kT. Not the legacy entropy-production p-value: that test is significant even on reversible ground truth, so a small p-value does not mean the process is out of equilibrium. Neither number is a physical dissipation rate in joules.

My real lineage has a cyclic fraction near the floor. Is the method broken? No. A linear lineage has an arrow of time (captured by the committor) but little circulation, so a near-reversible reading is the expected result. The measure's detection power is established on synthetic ground truth with a known drive.

Why is my landscape's raw free energy not a good pseudotime? Because it is not meant to be. The raw energy is the landscape; the commitment coordinate is the committor. Use developmental_coordinate, not fit.energies, for ordering.

Why does the committor beat PCA pseudotime on one dataset but not another? Ordering advantage depends on the geometry of the lineage. On a clean linear lineage, PCA already orders nearly perfectly and is hard to beat. See Limitations.

How big a dataset can it handle? Graph construction scales to tens of thousands of cells in seconds. The full diagnostic fit is practical to a few thousand cells; disable the cycle decomposition (enable_cycle_decomposition=False) for larger runs.

Is it deterministic? Yes, given a seed. Benchmarks report means and confidence intervals over seeded random subsamples, so they reproduce exactly.

How do I cite it? See CITATION.cff.

Something failed on my data. What now? Check report.warnings from analyze. Common causes: too few cells (need at least four), fewer than two features, or no cells matching your source_labels / target_labels. Open an issue with the shapes and the config.

docs.title: Getting started
docs.text: This walkthrough runs the whole pipeline and explains each output. It uses synthetic data so it needs no download; the same calls work on real data.

docs.title: 1. Make or load data
docs.text:
The pipeline takes an expression matrix and a velocity matrix of the same shape (cells x features), and optional per-cell labels.

from thermodynamic_waddington import make_synthetic_dataset

ds = make_synthetic_dataset(cells=200, genes=16, seed=7)
ds.expression, ds.velocity, ds.labels

For real data, load an h5ad and build a spliced/unspliced velocity proxy, or use scVelo dynamical velocity. See Concepts.

docs.title: 2. One call
docs.text:
analyze runs everything and returns a compact report.

from thermodynamic_waddington import analyze

labels = ds.labels
report = analyze(ds.expression, ds.velocity, labels=labels,
                 source_labels=[sorted(set(labels))[0]],
                 target_labels=[sorted(set(labels))[-1]])

report.irreversibility_cyclic_fraction    # calibrated irreversibility (Hodge)
report.irreversibility_cycle_affinity_kt  # cycle affinities in kT (Schnakenberg)
report.irreversibility_noise_matched_excess  # circulation beyond the data's own noise (~0 = reversible)
report.irreversibility_noise_matched_z
report.landscape_range_kt         # landscape depth in kT
report.committor_order            # cell types ordered by commitment
report.commitment_label           # where the committor crosses 0.5
report.commitment_barrier_kt      # commitment barrier in kT
report.warnings                   # anything the analysis had to skip

report.to_dict() and report.save("out.json") serialize it.

docs.title: 3. Or drive the pipeline directly
docs.text:
For the full landscape object and all diagnostics:

from thermodynamic_waddington import fit_landscape, FitConfig

cfg = FitConfig(neighbors=20, dimensions=6, seed=7)
fit = fit_landscape(ds.expression, ds.velocity, config=cfg, labels=ds.labels)

fit.energies         # per-cell effective free energy
fit.attractors       # detected attractor cells
fit.diagnostics["schnakenberg"]   # cycle decomposition
fit.diagnostics["entropy_production"]  # legacy Seifert EP, kept for comparison only

The legacy Seifert entropy-production test over-detects (see Benchmarks); use the calibrated measure below for irreversibility claims.

docs.title: 3b. Calibrated irreversibility
docs.text:
import numpy as np
from thermodynamic_waddington.graph import build_knn
from thermodynamic_waddington.irreversibility import (
    cyclic_irreversibility, cycle_affinities, cyclic_flow_per_cell,
)

pts, vel = np.asarray(ds.expression), np.asarray(ds.velocity)  # same space for both
graph = build_knn(pts, k=15)
cyclic_irreversibility(pts, vel, graph).cyclic_fraction
cycle_affinities(pts, vel, graph).rms_affinity_kt
cyclic_flow_per_cell(pts, vel, graph)   # where along the lineage circulation lives

docs.title: 4. The committor and the commitment barrier
docs.text:
from thermodynamic_waddington import (
    developmental_coordinate, commitment_profile, committor_free_energy_profile,
)

q = developmental_coordinate(fit, source_labels=["HSC"], target_labels=["erythroid"])
profile = commitment_profile(fit, ["HSC"], ["erythroid"])
pmf = committor_free_energy_profile(q)

profile.order            # cell types by mean committor
profile.commitment_label # where commitment happens
pmf.barrier_kt           # commitment barrier
pmf.barrier_q            # committor value at the transition state

docs.title: 5. Calibrate to kT
docs.text:
from thermodynamic_waddington import calibrate_fit

cal = calibrate_fit(fit)
cal.boltzmann_energy_range_kt   # landscape depth in kT
cal.r_squared                   # path-work vs density agreement

docs.title: Limitations and scope
docs.text: A method is trustworthy in proportion to how clearly it states where it works and where it does not. This page is that statement. None of it is hidden elsewhere.

docs.title: What is well supported
docs.text:
• A calibrated irreversibility measure. The Hodge cyclic fraction separates equilibrium from non-equilibrium ground truth (AUROC 1.00) and tracks a known drive monotonically, with a correct false-positive rate. This is the core, defensible methodological claim.
  • Real lineages are reversible within their noise. On pancreas, gastrulation erythroid, bone marrow erythroid, and the Drosophila testis germline, the noise-matched excess is -0.011 to -0.005 (|z| <= 1). Against the clean floor pancreas showed +0.05; the noise-matched null shows it is noise. Power on these near-1D geometries is low, so this is "no circulation detected", not proof of none.
  • The commitment barrier. 1.6 kT [1.4, 1.9] on pancreas across 8 subsamples.
  • Committor ordering on a long staged lineage. On Drosophila spermatogenesis the committor beats PC1 in 8/8 subsamples (0.78 vs 0.47).
  • The software. Deterministic given a seed, 230 unit tests, lint-clean CI, reproducible in one command, numeric core pinned to bit-identical outputs.

docs.title: What is dataset-dependent
docs.text: • Committor ordering. The committor recovers developmental order better than PCA pseudotime on pancreas but not on the gastrulation erythroid lineage, where plain PC1 wins (on Drosophila spermatogenesis it wins clearly). Do not present the committor as a universally better pseudotime; present it as a commitment coordinate tied to the thermodynamics.

docs.title: What did not survive calibration
docs.text:
• "Differentiation is strongly irreversible." An earlier version reported significant entropy production across three tissues from the Seifert permutation test. That test false-positives on equilibrium ground truth (FPR 1.0), so the reading is withdrawn; the calibrated measure shows near-reversible lineages instead. The legacy test remains in the package for comparison.
  • A clean floor mistakes noise for circulation. Against the noise-free radial floor, noisy equilibrium data false-positives every time (ground truth with measurement noise). Use noise_matched_irreversibility; its own limits: power falls with noise, and residuals are estimated from kNN neighbourhoods, so real circulation at the scale of a single neighbourhood is partly treated as noise (conservative).
  • A depth-confounded per-cell map. The per-cell cyclic-energy map (cyclic_flow_per_cell) grows with velocity magnitude; on the fly testis it produced a 7x "peak" that tracked sequencing depth. Use the magnitude-invariant cyclic_fraction_per_cell against a local floor instead.
  • Detection power on real geometry. Injecting a rotation into the real near-1D pancreas geometry barely moves the cyclic fraction, because a 1D structure has few cycles to carry circulation. Power is established on the 2D synthetic ground truth, not on these lineages.

docs.title: What did not replicate
docs.text: • Dentate gyrus neurogenesis. The legacy entropy-production signal did not replicate across seven independent tests, including a preregistered confirmatory test. This negative result is retained in RESEARCH_NOTE_entropy_production_pancreas.md. It defines a boundary of the method, not a bug.

docs.title: What is not claimed
docs.text:
• The free energy is not a molecular free energy. It is a density-based pseudopotential expressed in kT. Rare or under-sampled states read as high energy. Read barriers as a pseudopotential, and use the calibrated cyclic fraction (not the legacy p-value) for non-equilibrium claims.
  • RNA velocity is an input, not a truth. Results depend on the velocity model. Most benchmarks use an unspliced-minus-spliced proxy; one dynamical- velocity check is included. Broader velocity models remain to be tested.
  • Validation is not exhaustive. Three vertebrate tissues, Drosophila spermatogenesis, synthetic ground truth, and one documented negative. The fly analysis uses one library at ~10% read depth, and its commitment-driver genes are a ranking for follow-up, not causal evidence. More datasets, and ideally wet-lab confirmation, are needed before strong biological conclusions.

docs.title: How to use it responsibly
docs.text:
• Report the cyclic fraction with its noise-matched excess (and the clean floor for reference), not the legacy entropy-production p-value.
  • Treat kT barriers as pseudopotential barriers.
  • State the velocity model and preprocessing.
  • If applying to a new system, compute the gradient floor at the same sample size first; if the observed cyclic fraction is not above it, the system is not measurably irreversible under this method, and that is a valid result to report.

docs.title: A preregistered test
docs.text: A falsifiable prediction and its decision rule are written in advance in PREREGISTRATION_commitment.md, so the commitment claim can be confirmed or refuted by experiment rather than argued.
